Hi Chris — thanks for the question and the PO. Quick summary up front: when a customer purchases via AWS Marketplace (co-sell), the purchaser typically receives an invoice from AWS (AWS issues the invoice and collects payment), but the tax treatment and final remit details depend on the ordering path and buyer tax residency. Redwood receives payouts from AWS and we provide reporting to reconcile.

A few clarifying questions so we give finance an authoritative answer:
- Is AlphaApps purchasing under an AWS marketplace subscription or via a SaaS contract procured directly with AWS (both occur in AWS flows)?
- Is AlphaApps a US entity or registered outside the US for VAT? If outside the US, which country/registration number?
- Who in Finance will own receiving the invoice PDF (we can also enable a secondary delivery to ap@alphaapps.com)?

I've attached an example invoice stub so you can see the typical fields and the "Seller" line that will vary depending on whether AWS or Redwood is providing the invoice. Also attaching a W-9 template (US buyers typically request our W-9; non-US buyers sometimes request a W-8BEN-E from Redwood if they think of US-source withholding).

Next steps: once you confirm entity and PO path, I'll loop in our finance ops lead and AWS partner support to confirm the exact invoice entity and whether AWS will show Redwood as the supplier name on the invoice or only list product line items.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra

Chris — adding ops detail from the marketplace side. Hi Rishi.

Operationally:
- If the transaction was processed as an AWS Marketplace direct purchase (AWS as the seller of record), AWS will issue the invoice to AlphaApps and collect any applicable sales taxes/VAT. The invoice will show AWS as the billing entity; Redwood will appear in marketplace reporting and in the AWS billing console as the SaaS partner (sometimes as a product line item or as the "Third-party seller" depending on region).
- If the deal was executed via an AWS co-sell contract where Redwood is listed as the seller of record (less common without a full commercial agreement), Redwood would issue the invoice directly and collect tax based on the location / tax forms provided.

Tax forms:
- US buyers: we can provide a Redwood W-9 if your AP team needs seller tax info on file.
- Non-US buyers: if withholding is a concern, Redwood can provide W-8BEN-E (for entities) or we can confirm AWS handles any VAT/sales tax collection automatically in the Marketplace purchase.

Late breaking nuance: some customers (especially EU-headquartered companies) want Redwood's VAT number on the invoice for reclaim. In most AWS Marketplace flows AWS is the invoice issuer and will include AWS VAT handling; customers can also ask AWS to include the partner VAT number but that's customer/AWS enabled on a case-by-case basis.

If you want, we can open a joint ticket with AWS Marketplace support to force-confirm the invoice entity for this specific PO and request that AWS add Redwood's VAT/Tax ID to the invoice (if AWS supports that for your jurisdiction).

I've attached a short flow diagram of the co-sell invoice paths (AWS-invoice vs partner-invoice) — should help finance map where to send payment.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Marketplace Ops, Redwood Inference

Hi Chris — quick commercial notes from sales/legal perspective:

- If AlphaApps requires Redwood to be the invoice issuer (billing to Redwood rather than AWS), we can do that but it requires a short commercial addendum and may change payment terms (we typically move to net-30 or net-45 in direct-billing cases).
- For co-sell discounts or credits that were agreed on during AWS-led procurement, the normal pattern is: AWS issues invoice; Redwood issues a credit memo to AWS (or to you, depending on the agreement) which then shows up as a separate line item. That can complicate AR reconciliation, so we only do partner-invoice flows for larger enterprise deals.

Proposed next steps:
1) Confirm whether you need Redwood on the invoice (as a legal requirement for VAT reclaim).
2) If yes, sign the short MPA addendum (DocuSign link below) and we will engage legal to approve an invoice-as-Redwood flow.
3) Otherwise, I'll open the AWS Portal ticket with Ben and Rishi to get AWS to confirm the invoice seller and whether they can include our VAT ID on the AWS-issued invoice.
